content.title: About
content.content: Cranberry juice 100% is made from ripe cranberries without any added sugar, concentrates, or other fruit blends. The berries are harvested in northern regions where the climate promotes a high antioxidant content. The juice has a bright red color, a characteristic tart‑sweet taste, and a rich aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cranberries are among the most acidic berries, which is why they are often used as a natural preservative.
Cranberry juice is a traditional beverage in New England (USA) and Canada.
High levels of proanthocyanidins in cranberries help prevent bacterial biofilm formation in the urinary tract.
Cranberry vines grow on shrubs up to 1.5 m tall and prefer acidic, peat‑rich soils.
In the 19th century, cranberry juice was used as a remedy for colds and stomach ailments.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Cranberry juice contains proanthocyanidins and vitamin C, which help neutralize free radicals and support the immune system.

items.title: Supports urinary tract health
items.content: Proanthocyanidins inhibit bacteria from adhering to bladder walls, reducing the risk of infections.

items.title: May lower cardiovascular risk
items.content: Studies suggest regular consumption can improve lipid profiles and help lower blood pressure.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: The acidity stimulates gastric juice production, promoting better digestion.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: The juice provides small amounts of B1, B2, and B6, which are involved in energy metabolism.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: High acidity may irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Cranberry juice can enhance the effect of anticoagulants such as warfarin; consult a doctor if you take these medications.

items.title: Added sugars in some products
items.content: Some commercial versions contain added sugar; choose 100% pure juice without additives.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, individuals may experience an allergic reaction to cranberries.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Drink the juice chilled as a refreshing beverage, use it in smoothies, cocktails, or as a base for sauces and marinades. To reduce tartness, it is often diluted with water or apple juice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the juice in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. After opening, consume within 5–7 days. Avoid freezing, as it can alter flavor and texture.
